rows.description: A young adult decides when to be plain, especially for safety, consent, deadlines and boundaries, and when a gentle indirect phrase suits. Over-reliance on hints leaves needs unmet and others uncertain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young professional reads "That might be difficult" or "We will try" as possible refusal in some settings and as a real maybe in others. Following up with a clear question reduces misreading.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult attends another community's ceremony and greets in its way or keeps beliefs private. The same behaviour can signal belief, courtesy or curiosity, so intent cannot be assumed from participation alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult attends funerals or memorial rites, observes mourning periods and offers condolences in the family's manner. Customs on colour, food, speech and crying vary widely, so following the family's lead shows respect.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: admiration, sadness, grief

rows.description: Signers may vary signs across regions, generations and communities, such as Indian Sign Language, ASL or BSL, and may mix sign, speech and writing. Clarifying a sign is normal, not a failure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Sign language in workplaces and public life [Expressing]
rows.description: A young signer works through interpreters or video relay and expects equal access. Colleagues can learn a few signs, face the person and avoid assumptions about ability.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young professional drafts a hard message, waits before sending and reads it aloud for tone. Serious conflict, bad news or emotional topics often need a conversation instead of text.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Letters and poetry for meaning and memory [Expressing]
rows.description: A young adult writes condolence letters, farewell notes, poems or letters to a future self to mark feelings. Written words can be kept and reread, so they carry both comfort and permanence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult learns that emoji, gestures in pictures and memes carry different meanings across age groups and cultures, such as a thumbs-up or folded hands. Checking intent or asking avoids offence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young professional adjusts emoji, punctuation and reply speed for colleagues and clients, and uses clear subject lines. Norms differ by organisation and culture, so matching the recipient's style is wise.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
